intro: Five developments worth knowing. Not a summary of AI news—the few changes most likely to affect your teaching, research, methods, institution, or professional environment.

topics.title: From teaching AI use to evaluating student judgment
topics.changed: Michigan's Center for Academic Innovation announced faculty forums focused on AI roleplay, simulation, course redesign, tutoring and assessment.
topics.matter: In marketing analytics, students may increasingly produce sophisticated analyses without necessarily demonstrating that they understand them.
topics.action: Consider an assignment where students may use AI for analysis but must independently defend their methods, validation and managerial conclusions.

topics.title: AI consumer research is entering mainstream business infrastructure
topics.changed: Salesforce announced an agreement to acquire Listen Labs, whose AI agents conduct customer research and synthesize findings; Salesforce also highlights customer-behavior simulations.
topics.matter: AI-generated customer insight is moving beyond academic experiments into commercial marketing systems, raising questions about preference measurement, representation and validation.
topics.action: Watch how commercial systems demonstrate that simulated customer responses actually predict human behavior, especially under new conditions.

topics.title: Digital twins: richer interviews don't necessarily mean better predictions
topics.changed: A Columbia/Wharton working paper compared AI-moderated, human-moderated and static interviews with 317 participants. AI found more customer needs at a fixed budget, but its added conversational richness did not improve quantitative prediction over static interviews.
topics.matter: The distinction between generating qualitative insight and predicting behavior is highly relevant to quantitative marketing research—and a useful antidote to synthetic-consumer hype.
topics.action: Look closely at individual-level fidelity and how prediction deteriorates as validation questions move farther from the information used to construct the digital twin.

topics.title: Michigan is funding faculty experiments with AI
topics.changed: U-M is offering selected faculty projects up to $15,000 plus instructional-design, project-management and technical support for AI-supported teaching and learning experiments.
topics.matter: It creates a relatively low-friction path from discussing AI pedagogy to testing a concrete instructional idea with institutional support.
topics.action: Consider whether a bounded marketing-analytics experiment—perhaps AI-assisted analysis plus skills validation—would be worth proposing. Verify the current deadline before acting.
topics.sourceLabel: U-M AI Implementation Call for Proposals

topics.title: The interface to organizational work may be shifting from software to agents
topics.changed: Enterprise AI systems are increasingly being positioned as agents that carry out workflows rather than merely answer questions inside conventional software.
topics.matter: If employees increasingly direct agents rather than operate applications themselves, organizations may need to rethink training, job design, accountability and productivity measurement.
topics.action: Watch for evidence of improved completed work—not simply more AI usage. Adoption matters less than whether organizations actually redesign workflows around the technology.
